content:
BUILT CoLAB marked its first year of activity yesterday, 16 September. This year is marked, despite the pandemic, by the remarkable and consistent growth of this Collaborative Laboratory: both in terms of human resources and the operational and research results it set out to achieve.


In fact, over the last 12 months, BUILT CoLAB has come to have 24 staff members, split between the Porto and Lisbon offices, and has been involved in several highly diverse projects aligned with its research agenda. Of particular note is the coordination of the largest R&D&I project ever developed by the construction sector in Portugal, whose work is under way and aims to transform the AEC sector. With its 20 members, it has been developing specific work to develop solutions for digitalising work processes that increase its competitiveness in the market.


Also worth highlighting is the recognition BUILT CoLAB has already earned from its peers and the AEC sector in general, the result of excellent work carried out and an effective communication strategy, with outreach and “evangelisation” activities for digital construction and the energy and climate transition.


To successfully achieve the objectives it has set out to achieve, Paulo Fonseca, Executive Director of BUILT CoLAB, highlights the “fundamental role and support of the Board, Members and, in particular, the whole Team, who, combining experience and youth, have managed to carry out research and development work that is crucial for the project and for promoting highly qualified employment within and beyond BUILT CoLAB”. Paulo Fonseca also wants to extend “a word of appreciation to the funding entities, particularly ANI and FCT, whose support has been fundamental to the birth and growth of the project”.


Thus, bringing together centres of knowledge, industry and users in a collaborative environment, BUILT CoLAB wants to continue promoting a co-creation model that will drive the digital and climate transition of buildings and infrastructure, with a view to increasing productivity, competitiveness and sustainable growth in the AEC sector ecosystem, and contribute to transforming the built environment of the future.


This first year of activity was a significant step in that direction.
